title: 8-mark evaluate level descriptors
subject: Geography
source: Written for geography/y10 lesson 50 (8-mark evaluate level descriptors (portal printable))
intro: Lesson 50: Case study: managing the Holderness coast at Mappleton (2.3). Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

panels.title: The scheme, 1991
points: Rock revetment at the cliff foot

model.title: Evaluate the success of coastal management in a named developed area. (8 marks) Plan

parts.text: Intro: Mappleton, 1991, two rock groynes and revetment, about £2 million
Success: village and road protected; beach built up
Problems: terminal groyne effect at Cowden; sediment supply cut
Judgement: successful locally, less so for the whole coast

keywords.def: a groyne made of large boulders
rocks placed at a cliff foot to absorb waves
comparing a scheme's costs with what it protects
further along the coast in the direction of longshore drift
meeting needs now without harming the future

questions.q: Explain one negative effect of the Mappleton scheme. (2 marks)
questions.a: Groynes trapped sediment (1), so the coast to the south received less and eroded faster (1)

questions.q: Core: 'Evaluate the success of coastal management in a named area in a developed country.' (8 marks) Timed: 12 minutes in the portal response box.
questions.a: Level 3: detailed place knowledge, balanced, substantiated judgement

questions.q: Extend: Self-assess with the level descriptors and write one target.
questions.a: Accurate self-assessment with a specific target

questions.q: Stretch: Suggest a more sustainable plan for Holderness. (4 marks)
questions.a: Mix of managed retreat where land value is low, compensation for residents, protecting key settlements

options: Increased erosion beyond the last groyne
questions.a: B) Increased erosion beyond the last groyne. Sediment trapped by groynes no longer reaches the coast downdrift.

questions.q: Big question: did saving Mappleton cost someone else?
questions.a: Yes in part: downdrift erosion increased, showing management must consider the whole sediment cell
